0.6 rated; 0.74 measured by The Smart Home Hookup

products.warranty: 2 years on the screen, 5 years on the motor. You pay to ship the screen in for a claim; VIVIDSTORM pays to ship the repaired or replacement screen back.

products.summary: A motorized screen that rises out of a floor case, built for UST laser projectors. It was the best-performing and best-value floor-rising screen in The Smart Home Hookup's measured test.
products.fit: UST projector owners who want a big image in a lit living room and want the screen gone when it's off, with no drilling.
caveats: UST only. With a long-throw or ceiling-mounted projector, the image will look dim and uneven.
The price shown is for the smallest size. Larger sizes cost more.
Owners report motors that stopped and riser arms that snapped. Never force or pull on the screen to adjust it while it is raised.
In the test, the backing let in more light from behind than the NothingProjector screen did, which matters if a window is behind the screen.

notes: Query: 'floor rising projector screen'. Current results are mostly maker blogs (VIVIDSTORM, NothingProjector, AWOL), store listings and low-quality affiliate roundups. Only one independent measured comparison exists (The Smart Home Hookup). PAIN POINTS (approximate counts from sources read): motor stops, won't rise or heat cutoff 5 (Trustpilot 1, Trustpilot regional 1 motor failure under a year, Reddit owner of 3 units 1, dealer note about motor buzzing 1, maker troubleshooting blog 1); riser arm, leg or base breakage 4 (StereoNET snapped arm, NothingProjector blog claims S PRO legs broke after 3 years (rival claim), Trustpilot tilted base, Reddit missing screws/anti-pinch fault); wrinkles or creases 4 (2 Amazon reviews via Fakespot on the VIVIDSTORM Slimline, dealer note, maker's own humidity note); wrong surface for projector type 4+ (maker listings, Elite listing, guides, StereoNET note on throw ratio below 1.5); shipping, duties or claim shipping 3; support: 16 positive and 3 negative on Trustpilot page 1; weight 2. SEGMENTS: UST in a lit room goes to VIVIDSTORM S PRO (measured best performance and value: 0.74 gain, 80% rejection at 45°, 0.03 lux black floor). Window behind the screen goes to NothingProjector, which matched the S PRO in the test and has better rear backing; the article's tested NothingProjector model may not be the current Black Series. Long throw goes to VIVIDSTORM S ALR, cheapest long-throw ALR floor riser found (Elite CineGrey 4D from $1,923 at 122 in and up). PRICES: all from storecheck search (lowest-variant 'from' prices) on 2026-11-11. VIVIDSTORM S PRO $1,774, S PRO P $1,794, US Arizona S PRO Plus $1,533, S ALR $1,194. NothingProjector Black from $1,399 (84 in); its separate 120 in listing is $1,799. AWOL from $1,699. Elite TT2 CLR from $2,594; TT2 CLR3 121 in $2,864; TT3 CineGrey 4D from $1,923. NOT VERIFIED: per-size prices. storecheck product and WebFetch got HTTP 429 from every Shopify product page all session, so the size behind each 'from' price is assumed to be the smallest. The Arizona listing's sizes and colors are unknown. The S PRO 72-130 in size list comes from a store page listing block; the S ALR 72-200 in size list also comes from a store listing block. Returns: the store refund page body did not render. A search snippet said personal-reason returns get store credit minus 30% with the buyer paying shipping both ways; this is unverified and kept off the page. Warranty (2 years screen, 5 years motor, buyer pays inbound claim shipping) was read on vividstorm.us (Vividstorm USA LLC) and matches the '2-5-Year Warranty' banner on vividstormscreen.com. Weight of 49-75 lb is from Projector Reviews for an earlier S PRO. Gain, rise time, viewing angle and DC motor specs are maker claims. Codes: none from the network, and none found on the home page or the BFCM 2026 page. No Amazon records per the 2026-11-06 rule; no Amazon-only product wins a segment here.
